'''''Himantoglossum robertianum'''''  is a species of flowering plant in the orchid family ([[Orchidaceae]]) native to the [[Mediterranean Basin]]. It is commonly known as the '''giant orchid'''.

==Description==
''Himantoglossum robertianum'' is a [[bulb|bulbous plant]].<ref name="iberica">{{cite web |title=Himantoglossum robertianum |url=http://www.floraiberica.es/floraiberica/texto/pdfs/21_189_21_Barlia.pdf |publisher=[[Flora Iberica]] |access-date=17 December 2020}}</ref> It flowers from January to April.<ref name="iucn" /><ref name="flora-on" /> The bulb is edible when cooked.<ref name="iucn" />

==Distribution and habitat==
''Himantoglossum robertianum'' is native to the [[Mediterranean Basin]] and is found in [[Portugal]], [[Morocco]], [[Spain]], [[Balearic Islands]], [[France]], [[Italy]], [[Sardinia]], [[Corsica]], [[Algeria]], [[Libya]], [[Croatia]], [[Montenegro]], the [[Greece|Greek mainland]], the [[Aegean Islands]] and [[Crete]], [[Anatolia]] and [[Cyprus]],<ref name="CoL">{{cite web |title=Himantoglossum robertianum (Loisel.) P.Delforge |url=https://www.catalogueoflife.org/data/taxon/3LXXT |publisher=[[Catalogue of Life]] |access-date=17 December 2020}}</ref> and recently (March 2023) found in [[Palestine]].<ref name="NB">{{cite web |title=Himantoglossum robertianum (Loisel.) P.Delforge |url=https://israel.inaturalist.org/observations/150730217 |publisher=[[Catalogue of Life]] |access-date=12 March 2023}}</ref> It is found in short, poor grassland, [[garrigue]], scrub, and open woodland. It prefers dry to moist, alkaline and [[limestone|calcareous]] substrates.<ref name="flora-on">{{cite web |title=Barlia robertiana (Loisel.) Greuter |url=https://flora-on.pt/#/1Barlia+robertiana |publisher=Flora-on |access-date=17 December 2020}}</ref><ref name="iucn" /> It can be found up to {{convert|1700|m|ft|abbr=on}} altitude.<ref name="iucn" /> 
The plant was found growing in [[Great Britain|Britain]] for the first time in 2022. It is believed that its distribution range is expanding due to the effects of climate change.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2022/apr/01/giant-orchids-found-growing-wild-in-uk-for-first-time|title=Giant orchids found growing wild in UK for first time|website=[[TheGuardian.com]]|date=April 2022}}</ref>
